findings.location: Boundaries & Constraints > Never ("headless config copy/`reached`/`not reached`") vs Always (Configured cells, Aggregate configured versions)
findings.issue: The slice makes the configured set come only from the `--config` JSON (plan and aggregate ignore `--versions`/`--browsers` for it; aggregate versions come from config) but defers the Headless rule that writes the caller's versions and browsers into `<module>-psm-config.headless.<session>.json`. Today headless.md takes versions and browsers from the caller's arguments. After this slice, a psm-develop/psm-cross-version/psm-scaffold/psm-optimize call that narrows to, say, 9.1 × chromium is judged against the resolver's 3×2 set, so `ready` is always false. Under the contract the aggregate's differing `--versions` is also exit 2.
findings.implementation_impact: Every narrowed headless caller regresses to permanent `ready=false` (or exit 2) as soon as the slice merges. The per-version verdict contract that SPEC.md Constraints says headless callers keep is broken in the interim.
findings.suggestion: Pull the headless config-copy bullet (cell-contract.md > Headless, first bullet) into this slice, since it is pure config plumbing. Or state an explicit interim rule (e.g. headless passes a config whose `psm_target_versions`/`psm_e2e_browsers` equal its arguments) and add a test for a narrowed headless call.

findings.location: Boundaries > Never (CAP-1: `e2e_step`, `phase1_reuse`, run scope; `--tier`) + Always (`--per-version` is exit 2 for layer e2e) + Tasks > docs ("Fase 1/2 e2e commands")
findings.issue: The slice removes today's E2E orchestration path: run-phases.md Fase 1 gates on `all_reuse` and Fase 2 runs `--layer e2e --per-version --jobs N`, then `--merge-only` when `all_reuse` is true. But it defers everything the contract uses to replace it (`phase1_reuse`, `e2e_step`, `e2e_next_cells`, `e2e_cells_arg`, `--tier`). The spec never says what the Phase 1/Phase 2 E2E procedure is in this intermediate state. It does not say how the orchestrator builds `--cells`, which plan field ends a Phase 1 loop, or when Phase 2 starts. The docs task names the sections to edit but gives no content.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer must invent an interim orchestration, and the contract forbids exactly that ("the orchestrator ... never picks a tier by judgment"). The likely result is SKILL.md/run-phases.md text that hand-derives `--cells` from `rerun_matrix`. That text gets rewritten in CAP-1, and until then interactive runs have no defined convergence path.
findings.suggestion: Add a short 'Interim orchestration (until CAP-1)' section: the exact Phase 1 and Phase 2 E2E commands, how `--cells` is formed from the e2e `rerun_matrix` entries, which boolean gates loop exit and Phase 2 entry, and that `--merge-only --layer e2e` is the report view only.

findings.location: Always ("Plan's per-cell `rerun_matrix` reasons") vs cell-contract.md > Plan ("`all_reuse` keeps today's computation over these `rerun` lists") vs ps-plan-layers.py `per_version_rollup`
findings.issue: The contract says e2e `rerun_matrix` entries cover every configured cell whatever `--versions`, while `per_version[V].rerun` lists e2e only for V. Today `per_version_rollup` computes `all_reuse = not matrix`. If that stays, a Phase 1 call for `--versions V --per-version` can never report `all_reuse: true` while any other version's or Firefox's cell is stale. If `all_reuse` is recomputed from the `rerun` lists, it can be true while `rerun_matrix` is non-empty. Phase 1 still gates on `all_reuse` in this slice because `phase1_reuse` is deferred.
findings.implementation_impact: Depending on which reading the implementer picks, Phase 1 per-version loops either never converge or report convergence while the matrix shows reruns. Either way existing per_version_rollup tests break in an unspecified direction.
findings.suggestion: State explicitly how `all_reuse` is computed in this slice: from `per_version[*].rerun` only, or excluding e2e entries for versions outside `--versions`. Add a test: config 3×2, `--versions 9.1 --per-version`, 9.1 fully fresh, 8.1 e2e stale → expected `all_reuse` and `rerun_matrix`.

findings.location: I/O & Edge-Case Matrix row 'Narrowed plan' + Always ("browser-keyed `layers.e2e`") vs ps-plan-layers.py canonical mode
findings.issue: Canonical (non-`--per-version`) plan output has no `rerun_matrix` today; only per-version mode emits it, via `per_version_rollup`. The 'Narrowed plan' row and the contract ('per-cell planning in both modes') assume one exists, but the spec does not say whether canonical mode gains a `rerun_matrix`, what its non-e2e entries look like, or which mode the row tests.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer either adds a new canonical `rerun_matrix` with a shape nobody specified or tests the row only in per-version mode. Canonical-mode per-cell freshness (used by Phase 2) is then left unverified.
findings.suggestion: Specify that canonical mode gains `rerun_matrix`, and give its shape (same `{layer, version, browser?, reason?, per_version_capable}` entries). Split the 'Narrowed plan' row into canonical and per-version cases.

findings.location: Always ("browser-keyed `layers.e2e`"); Tasks > ps-plan-layers.py
findings.issue: The shape of each browser entry under `layers.e2e` / `per_version[V].layers.e2e` is never defined. Today each layer entry is `plan_layer`'s `{reuse, reason, path}`. Canonical `rerun` is computed as `[l for l, p in plans.items() if not p['reuse']]`, and `plan_per_version` does the same per version. A dict keyed by browser has no `reuse` key.
findings.implementation_impact: Existing `rerun` computation breaks (KeyError, or e2e silently treated as reuse). Readers (run-phases.md, tests) get an ad-hoc per-browser shape that may not match what CAP-1 later expects.
findings.suggestion: Define the per-browser entry, e.g. `{reuse: bool, reason: <contract reason>|null, history: <path>}`. State that e2e's `rerun` membership derives from 'any browser entry has reuse=false'.

findings.location: Boundaries > Never ("`stopped` records") vs cell-contract.md > Evidence record > Storage
findings.issue: Stopped records are deferred, but the spec gives no rule for what ps-run-layer appends when it is stopped via `--stop-job` (exit 143) or the child is killed. By the Storage rule, a child that left no result produces an `inconclusive` record with reason `crash`, so an operator stop is recorded as a crash. In the contract, `stopped` is explicitly skipped by `blocked-infra`, while `crash` counts as an infra cause.
findings.implementation_impact: Histories written by this slice carry false `crash` records for every operator stop. Once CAP-1 lands, two such records in one session on one fingerprint yield a spurious `blocked-infra` and end the E2E loop.
findings.suggestion: Either include the `stopped` record (written from the stop handler) in this slice, or state that a run ending in 143 appends no record for unfinished cells. Add an I/O matrix row for --stop-job during a run.

findings.location: Always ("prints the Runner > Output JSON line; exit 3/1/0/2/143 per Runner") vs Never ("`not-run` production" deferred to CAP-3)
findings.issue: Runner > Output says a child exit 2 makes the remaining queued cells `not-run` with reason `input-error after <ver>`, in-flight children finish, and ps-run-layer exits 2. This slice defers `not-run` production and keeps `--jobs` concurrency. The spec does not say what happens to the other queued versions' cells when one child exits 2 (run anyway? cancelled with no record?), or what `appended` reports.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer must choose between partially building CAP-3 (forbidden: 'do not half-build') and silently diverging from the Runner rule it was told to implement 'as written'.
findings.suggestion: Add an explicit interim rule for child exit 2: e.g. no new child starts, queued cells get no record, `appended` lists only records actually written, exit 2. Add it to the I/O matrix.

findings.location: Never ("`--tier` (record `tier: null`)") vs Tasks > docs (e2e-quickstart TDD verdict step) and cell-contract.md > Runner input errors
findings.issue: cell-contract.md > Docs, which the spec points to, gives the quickstart TDD verdict step as `ps-run-layer.py --layer e2e --cells … --tier 0 --session <token>`. Its Runner input errors also make 'a `--tier` missing' exit 2. This slice adds no `--tier` flag, so argparse rejects `--tier 0` (it comes before `--`). The spec says neither that the missing-`--tier` error is not enforced nor what the slice's TDD command is.
findings.implementation_impact: Docs copied from the contract give a command that fails with exit 2. Alternatively the implementer adds a `--tier` flag to make the docs work, which half-builds CAP-1.
findings.suggestion: Give the exact slice-level TDD verdict command (`--layer e2e --cells 9.1:chromium --session <t>` then `ps-aggregate.py --reports-dir … --module … --config …`). State that the `--tier` input-error rule is deferred along with the flag.

findings.location: Always ("plan and aggregate accept `--session` optionally (validated, unused this slice)") vs cell-contract.md > Evidence record > Fields (`session`)
findings.issue: The contract says the token is 'passed as `--session` to every plan call and every `ps-run-layer.py --layer e2e` run; both reject a missing or malformed token (exit 2)'. Making it optional on the plan changes a contract rule rather than deferring a capability, and the spec's own Ask First reserves that for the human.
findings.implementation_impact: Plan callers written in this slice (docs, headless) will omit `--session`. CAP-1 then has to tighten the flag to required, which breaks every caller written against the slice.
findings.suggestion: Make `--session` required (exit 2 when missing or malformed) on plan calls now, as the contract says; it costs nothing. Or record the deviation explicitly as approved by the human.

findings.location: Design Notes ("Boot `wall_clock` is taken after `_teardown` returns ... an outer wrapper measures") + Approach (CAP-6)
findings.issue: The boot's `wall_clock` has no defined start point. An outer wrapper around `run_one_version` measures the whole version run, browser phases included. CAP-6's purpose is to show whether boot or browser driving dominates. A boot wall-clock that contains the browser phases makes that comparison meaningless.
findings.implementation_impact: `e2e_phase_durations.boots[*].wall_clock` will roughly equal the sum of boot and browser time. Operators and the later timing report (SPEC Success signal) read a boot cost inflated by browser time.
findings.suggestion: Define boot `wall_clock` precisely: either from the first container phase (`pull` or `bring-up`) to the end of `teardown`, documented as including browser time, or as elapsed container-phase time excluding `browser:*`. State what the cell's own `wall_clock` covers relative to it.

findings.location: Design Notes ("one sink per version process") + Tasks > ps-flashlight-run.py (`phase` timing sink) + I/O row 'Timings'
findings.issue: `ps-e2e-run.py main` loops over several versions in one process for direct runs, and the spec keeps per-version `boot_phases`/`cells` in the child shape. A per-process sink accumulates phases across versions, and `boot_id` = process RUN_ID repeats for every version's boot. `fl.phase` is also used by Layer 2 (`install+phpstan`) and Layer 5 (`snapshot-db`, `scenario`), and the sink activation rule is unspecified. Ordinary e2e boots also produce suffixes the matrix does not cover: `pull#2` (PS and DB images), and `bring-up#2`/`teardown#2` after the port-conflict retry.
findings.implementation_impact: Direct multi-version runs report merged or duplicated phases and colliding boot_ids. A sink left active, or global, could leak into flashlight/scenario runs. Retry suffixes may be emitted inconsistently.
findings.suggestion: Specify a sink opened and closed per `run_one_version` call (per boot), inactive by default so Layers 2 and 5 are unaffected. Define `boot_id` per boot, which is unique even in a multi-version process. Add matrix rows for the two-image pull and the port-retry case.

findings.location: Tasks > `ps-e2e-run.py` bullet vs Always ("Producers ... as written")
findings.issue: The task list omits several Producer and Field obligations the contract places on the child. Per-engine `launch_error` is one: today a launch failure becomes a version-level `browser_notes` line and the engine is dropped. Each finding's new `action` and `step` (0-based step index) are another; today's `assemble_findings` emits neither `step` nor a per-finding `action`. Per-cell `bo_authed` and `scenarios_run` are also missing. The probe-missed note currently lands in version-level `browser_notes`, and the spec does not say it must stay out of the other engine's cell.
findings.implementation_impact: An implementer working from the task list produces cells whose launch failures read as reason `not-driven` or `browser-notes` instead of `launch-error`. Findings lack the (scenario, step, action) key CAP-4/CAP-7 rely on, and a probe-missed chromium note could drop a firefox cell's passing grade.
findings.suggestion: Extend the ps-e2e-run.py task to name `launch_error` per cell, findings `action`+`step`, per-cell `bo_authed`, `scenarios_run` (or explicitly null), and the rule that probe or launch notes go only to their own engine's cell. Add a test for each.

findings.location: Always (Aggregate: "legacy `<module>-e2e*.json` ignored") + ("`--merge-only` report view") vs ps-aggregate.py `main` file discovery
findings.issue: `ps-aggregate.py main` auto-derives `<module>-<layer>.json` for every layer in LAYERS when `--reports-dir` is given, e2e included. This slice makes `--merge-only --layer e2e` write `<module>-e2e.json` (the `view: true` report view) into that same folder. The spec does not say that the auto-discovery loop must drop e2e. It also does not say how the aggregate behaves without `--reports-dir`/`--module`, as in today's quickstart form `--static static.json --e2e e2e.json`, where no histories can be located.
findings.implementation_impact: The aggregate either loads the report view as E2E evidence, which is a verdict from a non-evidence file, or trips the new `--e2e` exit 2 through discovery. Explicit-path aggregate calls get undefined E2E behaviour.
findings.suggestion: State that e2e is removed from the derived-file loop and that the history reader requires `--reports-dir` + `--module`. Say what happens without them (e.g. every cell `missing`, or exit 2 when `--require` includes e2e). Add a test with a `view: true` `<module>-e2e.json` present.

findings.location: Always ("`ps-run-layer.py --config` for every layer ... Layer `e2e`: exactly one of `--cells`/`--versions`") vs ps-run-layer.py argparse
findings.issue: The spec underspecifies the ps-run-layer argument changes. `--versions` is `required=True` for all layers today, and the spec does not say it becomes optional only for e2e. `merge_only` requires `--versions`, while the contract's e2e report view takes only `--module`, `--reports-dir`, `--config`. The spec also does not list which `--config` keys ps-run-layer itself reads in this slice (configured set and tag map, but not slots, canary or TTL). And it does not say that ps-run-layer must not use `apply_config_file`, which would fill `--versions` from `psm_target_versions`.
findings.implementation_impact: Likely bugs: `--cells` runs rejected for missing `--versions`; `--merge-only --layer e2e` still demanding `--versions`; or `apply_config_file` silently widening an e2e run to every configured version.
findings.suggestion: Add an explicit flag matrix for ps-run-layer in this slice: required/optional per layer and mode, the keys read from `--config` via its own key map, and `--merge-only --layer e2e` accepting no `--versions`/passthrough.

findings.location: Always (Producers: ps-run-layer resolves each version's `image_tag`) + Code Map (child emits `image_tag`)
findings.issue: Both ps-run-layer, from its passthrough `--tag-map`/`--extra-tag-map` and `psm_flashlight_tag_map` in `--config`, and the child, through `apply_config_file` plus the forwarded passthrough, resolve the tag. The spec does not say which value is written into the merged record or what happens when they differ.
findings.implementation_impact: If the child's tag is stamped and differs from the tag plan and aggregate resolve (e.g. the tag map arrives only through `--config` on one side), every record reads `stale-tag` forever. The opposite choice stamps a tag the container never ran.
findings.suggestion: State that the child's `image_tag` is authoritative for records it produced, and that ps-run-layer compares it with its resolved tag. Treat a mismatch as an input error or an inconclusive record. Add a test.

findings.location: Tasks & Acceptance > Acceptance Criteria
findings.issue: The three ACs are thin and partly untestable. 'ready holds the E2E part true' does not define an assertable output. 'All six cells' assumes a 3×2 config that is never stated. Not covered: exit code 3 vs 1 for child and runner; `--new-session` output (`[a-z0-9]{16}`, other flags exit 2); `--e2e` exit 2; legacy `<module>-e2e*.json` ignored; the removed `unscanned` gate (narrowed Layer 1 gives ready=false, not exit 2); `incomplete-record`; `not_run_cells`; per-version `e2e_state`/`reason`; the `--engines` override.
findings.implementation_impact: Large parts of the Always list can be skipped or mis-implemented while all ACs pass, and the reviewer has no measurable done-criterion for them.
findings.suggestion: Rewrite AC1 with explicit inputs (config 3×2) and outputs (`e2e_cells` all passing gate-grade, `versions[*].e2e_state == pass`, `e2e_phase_durations[ver].boots` with exactly one entry per boot_id). Add ACs for each exit-code path, `--new-session`, `--e2e`, legacy files, the unscanned-gate removal and incomplete records.

findings.location: Frontmatter `context` (omits tier-matrix.md) + Boundaries > Never
findings.issue: The Never list defers tier concepts (`e2e_step`, focus, canary, `blocked-*`, run scope) defined in tier-matrix.md, yet the frontmatter context loads only SPEC.md, cell-contract.md and brownfield.md. Some in-scope rerun reasons also depend on Plan definitions (`not-gradeable`, `scenario-notes` against the plan's current `e2e_scenario_notes`) that the slice must implement without the surrounding tier machinery. The spec does not mark which Plan sub-definitions are in scope.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer may stop at the `cell-contract.md` > Plan heading and skip `not-gradeable`/`scenario-notes` because they sit in the deferred tier text. Or they may build the failing/focus definitions because the reason list references them (e.g. aggregate `stale-fail` needs 'failing').
findings.suggestion: List the exact Plan sub-definitions in scope (rerun reasons, not-gradeable, failing as used by `stale-fail`) and those out of scope. Add tier-matrix.md to the context, or state why it is unnecessary.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md:32 (Never: headless config copy) vs :24 (Configured cells, aggregate --config)
findings.issue: Headless config copy is deferred, but configured cells now come only from --config. The spec does not say what headless callers (psm-develop, psm-cross-version, psm-scaffold, psm-optimize) pass in this slice when they narrow versions or browsers.
findings.implementation_impact: A headless call for one version gets ready=false from cells it never asked for. An aggregate call that still passes the caller's --versions hits the new exit 2 for a --versions that differs from config. Either way the per-version verdict contract of the headless callers breaks.
findings.suggestion: State the interim headless rule. Either pull the config-copy step into this slice, or say that headless keeps its current behavior and never passes --versions to the aggregate, and spell out which configured set applies.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md:32 (Never: e2e_step/e2e_next_cells/run scope) and :69 (docs: Fase 1/2 e2e commands)
findings.issue: e2e_step and e2e_next_cells are deferred, yet the docs task rewrites the Fase 1/2 E2E commands. The spec never says how the orchestrator turns the new per-cell rerun_matrix entries into a --cells or --versions argument.
findings.implementation_impact: SKILL.md and run-phases.md will say something the scripts do not decide. The orchestrator may pick cells by judgment, rerun browsers that already pass, or pass an argument the new rules reject (--per-version).
findings.suggestion: Give the interim rule. For example: group the layer-e2e rerun_matrix entries by version into --cells <ver>:<b>[+<b>] (one invocation, default --jobs), and use no other source of cells.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md:26 (layer e2e input errors) vs cell-contract.md Runner > Input errors
findings.issue: Only some of the contract's Runner input errors are named for this slice (one of --cells/--versions, and --per-version). The status of the others is left open: --tier missing or invalid, --jobs, --warm, --scenarios-from-failed, a repeated version in --cells, a cell outside the configured set, --cells with another layer.
findings.implementation_impact: One implementer may add a required --tier because the contract says so, which breaks every documented command. Another may accept repeated versions or cells outside the configured set, which writes histories that no reader looks at.
findings.suggestion: List every Runner input error explicitly, each with in-slice or deferred: --tier absent and rejected by argparse; --jobs accepted; repeated version, outside-config cell and --cells with another layer are exit 2.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md:69 (docs: e2e-quickstart.md TDD verdict step)
findings.issue: The contract's TDD verdict command includes --tier 0, but --tier is deferred. The spec does not say which form the quickstart doc should use.
findings.implementation_impact: A doc copied from the contract tells users to run a command that exits 2 on an unknown flag.
findings.suggestion: Say that the quickstart step in this slice is `ps-run-layer.py --layer e2e --cells … --session <token>` with no --tier, followed by `ps-aggregate.py --reports-dir`.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md:26,32 (exit 143; Never: stopped records)
findings.issue: ps-run-layer is stopped with --stop-job while children run. stopped records are deferred, and the spec does not say what ps-run-layer appends for the admitted cells.
findings.implementation_impact: The children exit 143 with no output, so the generic no-result path appends crash records. A crash record is an infra cause, so an operator stop later counts toward blocked-infra. The other option, appending nothing, is also unstated.
findings.suggestion: State the rule: when the run is stopped (JobStopped or SIGTERM), append no record for cells without a child result, and do not apply the crash rule to children killed by that stop.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md:27 (ps-e2e-run per-engine cells) / :44 (Crash child)
findings.issue: Some version-level failures happen before any engine is driven: skipped_image, compose unavailable, bring-up error, port-conflict retry, not healthy, install failure, no HTTP. The spec does not say whether the child still emits cells for every requested engine in these cases.
findings.implementation_impact: When cells is empty, ps-run-layer finds no per-cell result and writes crash. The real reason (errors or install) is lost, and the copy of errors and install into each cell, which the contract requires, never happens.
findings.suggestion: Require the child to emit `cells[engine] = {driven: false, launch_error: null, ...}` for every engine in --engines on every return path after the probe. Reserve crash for children that produce no parseable output.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md:26,66 (record merge in history mode)
findings.issue: The child output may name a version not requested, carry cells for an engine that was not admitted, lack a cell for an admitted engine, or fail validate_layer_shape. Today these cases cause exit 2 (rejected) or a missing-version result. History mode has no rule for them.
findings.implementation_impact: Stray records could be appended to the wrong cell's history, or an admitted cell could silently get no record. The exit code would be unpredictable.
findings.suggestion: Write the rule: ignore and log any cell outside the admitted set; give an admitted engine with no cell a crash record; treat output that fails the shape gate as no output, so the crash rule applies.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md:26 (child exit 2 under --jobs)
findings.issue: One child exits 2 while other version children are queued or running under --jobs. not-run production is deferred, and the spec does not say whether the others start or whether their records are appended.
findings.implementation_impact: Following today's code (return 2 before writing) drops valid records from the children that finished. Following the contract would need not-run records, which this slice cannot produce.
findings.suggestion: State the rule: queued children still run; every other child's records are appended; the exit-2 version gets no record; ps-run-layer exits 2 after appending.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md:26 (--versions for layer e2e)
findings.issue: ps-run-layer --layer e2e --versions 9.2 (not configured) or --versions 9.1.0 when 9.1 is configured. Exact-string matching is required only for canary and --cells versions.
findings.implementation_impact: A history named with a non-configured string (for example -9.1.0-) is never read, so the run looks successful but is invisible to plan and aggregate. Plan --per-version --versions 9.2 would also emit browser-keyed e2e for a version that is not configured.
findings.suggestion: Extend the exact configured-string match to ps-run-layer --versions for e2e (exit 2), and say how plan and aggregate treat a --versions entry outside the configured set.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md:24 (Configured cells read from --config)
findings.issue: --config is given, but psm_target_versions or psm_e2e_browsers is absent, null or an empty string. The spec does not say whether this means the script defaults or an empty list (exit 2). Reading or parsing the --config file can also fail.
findings.implementation_impact: Plan, runner and aggregate may resolve different configured sets from the same file, so cells planned as required do not match the cells the aggregate gates on.
findings.suggestion: State in the normalizer: key absent or null means the script default; a present empty string means exit 2; an unreadable or non-object config means exit 2. Use this one function in all three scripts.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md:24 (State/freshness incl. reports-dir exclusion) vs Runner input errors
findings.issue: The fingerprint rule depends on rejecting psm_reports_dir equal to the module root, and a passthrough --screenshot-dir inside the module but outside the reports dir. The spec does not list these Runner input errors, or the equivalent checks in plan and aggregate, as in scope.
findings.implementation_impact: Screenshots written inside the module change the fingerprint during every run, so every new record is stale the moment it is written. A reports dir at the module root makes the exclusion ambiguous.
findings.suggestion: Name both checks as in-slice exit 2 in ps-run-layer, plus the reports-dir check in plan and aggregate, wherever source_fingerprint is computed.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md:26 (history append, sole writer)
findings.issue: Appending to a history fails: OSError, disk full, flock error, or a reports dir that is missing or read-only.
findings.implementation_impact: The exit code is unspecified. Some cells may be recorded and others not, and the output line's `appended` list may claim records that were never written.
findings.suggestion: Write the rule: on append failure, log the path, leave it out of `appended`, keep appending the other cells, and exit 2 (or the stated code) after all cells are tried.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md:26 (--merge-only report view)
findings.issue: In --merge-only --layer e2e, the view value for a configured cell with no history, or with corrupt-history, is not stated. Nor is what happens when --versions or --session is also passed.
findings.implementation_impact: The view's shape is inconsistent (missing key vs null vs a placeholder). If --versions is still required by argparse, the contract's form of the command (no --versions) cannot run.
findings.suggestion: Define it: a cell with no valid record gets `cells[ver][b] = null`; --versions and --session are rejected with exit 2, or ignored (choose one); --versions is not required for layer e2e.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md:24 (Aggregate history-based E2E) / ps-aggregate.py main
findings.issue: The aggregate is called with explicit --static and no --reports-dir or --module, which the CLI still allows.
findings.implementation_impact: There is no history location, so every cell reads as missing with no error, or the code fails on a None path.
findings.suggestion: Make --reports-dir and --module required whenever the E2E layer is evaluated, or exit 2 when e2e is in --require and they are absent.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md:24 (aggregate per-version e2e_state/reason, reason as in plan)
findings.issue: A version has cells with different reasons, for example chromium missing and firefox stale-source. Plan reasons such as not-gradeable and scenario-notes also need the current e2e_scenario_notes, and the spec does not say whether the aggregate computes them.
findings.implementation_impact: The aggregate may report a different reason than the plan for the same cell, or pick an arbitrary cell's reason for versions[ver].reason.
findings.suggestion: State that versions[ver].reason is the reason of the first cell without passing evidence, in psm_e2e_browsers order. State that the aggregate computes current e2e_scenario_notes through the same discover_scenarios loader the plan uses.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md:41 (Corrupt line) and aggregate record selection
findings.issue: The last line of a history is corrupt and an earlier valid line is a passing gate-grade record. Aggregate selection still picks that pass.
findings.implementation_impact: e2e_cells shows state pass with gate_grade true next to reason corrupt-history. Consumers reading `state` may treat the cell as proven.
findings.suggestion: Say that when corrupt-history applies, e2e_cells[ver][b] gets gate_grade false and state inconclusive, with reason corrupt-history, whatever the selected record says.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md:63,78 (timing sink)
findings.issue: The timing sink has gaps. A direct ps-e2e-run.py run with several --versions holds several versions in one process. A phase can exit by exception (JobStopped, timeout). And the outcome values are not listed.
findings.implementation_impact: Phases from one version leak into the next one's boot_phases as #2 entries. The outcome strings may not match between producers and tests.
findings.suggestion: Reset the sink per run_one_version call. Enumerate outcome as ok, the phase status string, or error on exception, and record the entry in __exit__ whatever the outcome. Make the sink a no-op when inactive (Layer 2/5 phases).

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md:26-27 (image_tag Producers)
findings.issue: The child's emitted image_tag differs from the tag ps-run-layer resolved from its passthrough and config tag map.
findings.implementation_impact: The spec does not say which value the merged record stores. Freshness may then compare against a tag that was not actually booted, or reject valid evidence.
findings.suggestion: Write the rule: the child's image_tag wins in the merge; a mismatch with ps-run-layer's resolved tag is logged, and the record keeps the child value so it reads stale-tag.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md:24 (normalizer) vs Never (canary/CAP-1)
findings.issue: The config sets psm_e2e_canary outside the configured cells, or malformed. The canary is deferred, but the normalizer text mentions canary matching.
findings.implementation_impact: Some scripts in this slice may exit 2 on the canary and others may ignore it, so the same config is valid for plan but rejected by the aggregate, or the other way round.
findings.suggestion: State whether psm_e2e_canary is validated in this slice. Recommended: ignored by all three scripts until CAP-1.

findings.location: Boundaries > Always (Phase timings) + Design Notes; cell-contract.md > Evidence record > Fields / Phase timings
findings.issue: The record has one flat `wall_clock` field (Fields list). Phase timings gives the boot its own wall_clock ('boot_phases with the boot's own wall_clock') and also defines the cell's `wall_clock` as finished_at minus started_at. Aggregate `e2e_phase_durations.boots[<boot_id>].wall_clock` needs the boot value from each record. No field name for the boot wall-clock exists except inside `keeper_boot`. The spec's child list ('per-engine cells + boot_phases, wall_clock') does not say which one `wall_clock` is.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer has to invent where the boot wall-clock lives: overwrite the cell's wall_clock, nest it in boot_phases, or add a new field. Aggregate, tests and the bankwire timing report then disagree on what `wall_clock` means.
findings.suggestion: Name both explicitly, for example record `wall_clock` = cell (finished_at - started_at) and `boot_wall_clock` (or `boot_phases` = {phases, wall_clock}). State which one the aggregate reads for `boots` and which for `browsers`.

findings.location: Execution task ps-flashlight-run.py ('make `phase` record `{seconds, outcome}`'); cell-contract.md > Phase timings
findings.issue: `outcome` has no value set and `seconds` has no type. Today `phase.__exit__` writes END statuses 'ok', 'timeout', 'error(<Exc>)', or any free-form `ph.status` ('gagal', 'timeout(sisa-artefak: jalankan --cleanup-orphans)'). `_elapsed()` returns int seconds. Nothing says whether `outcome` copies that string or maps it to an enum, or whether seconds is an int or a float.
findings.implementation_impact: Tests and the aggregate's `e2e_phase_durations` get an unstable shape. Sub-second phases rounded to int read as 0, which undermines 'see whether boot or browser driving dominates'.
findings.suggestion: Define `seconds` as a float (for example monotonic, rounded to 3 decimals) and `outcome` as an enum (ok|timeout|error|failed), with the free-form status kept elsewhere or dropped.

findings.location: Boundaries > Always (`ps-e2e-run.py`: per-engine cells) + I/O row 'Crash child'; cell-contract.md > Evidence record > Storage / Fields sub-bullet 'engine never started'
findings.issue: When the boot fails (image missing, wait-healthy timeout, install failure, wait-http unreachable), today's `run_one_version` returns early with version-level `errors` and no per-engine data. Storage says ps-run-layer writes `crash` 'when the child left none'. So unless the child emits a `cells` entry for every engine even when no engine started, an install failure becomes a `crash` record instead of reason `install`/`errors`. The sub-bullet also says such cells get `started_at` = 'when ps-run-layer admitted it', which the child cannot know. Nothing says who builds these records.
findings.implementation_impact: Two plausible implementations produce different reasons for the same infra failure. Infra-cause classification later (blocked-infra) and the I/O 'Crash child' test both depend on it.
findings.suggestion: State that the child always emits `cells.<engine>` for every requested engine on every path after the probe, with `started_at`/`finished_at` null when the engine never started. ps-run-layer then fills started_at/finished_at (its spawn time and its write time) for those cells and for crash records.

findings.location: I/O row 'Probe drop'; Boundaries > Always (ps-run-layer record merge + crash/browser-unavailable records); cell-contract.md > Storage
findings.issue: ps-run-layer must write `browser-unavailable` for 'an engine the binary probe dropped', but the probe runs inside the child (`main`: `usable = [e for e in requested if browser_available(e)]`). The spec does not say which child output field tells ps-run-layer that an engine was probe-dropped rather than lost to a crash. Today the candidates are top-level `browsers_available`, the version-level `browser_notes` text, and `skipped_browser`.
findings.implementation_impact: Without a defined signal, ps-run-layer either parses free-text notes or labels every missing engine `crash`, which breaks the 'Probe drop' row.
findings.suggestion: Specify the signal, for example a child top-level `browsers_available` list or `cells.<engine> = {"state": "inconclusive", "reason": "browser-unavailable"}` emitted by the child. State that ps-run-layer maps a missing engine to `browser-unavailable` only when that signal says so, and to `crash` otherwise.

findings.location: Boundaries > Always ('exit 3/1/0/2/143 per Runner', 'Runner > Output JSON line') vs Never ('not-run production' deferred); cell-contract.md > Runner > Output
findings.issue: Runner > Output, which the spec imports, says a child exit 2 'stops queued cells as fail-fast does (`not-run`, reason `input-error after <ver>`), in-flight children finish, and ps-run-layer exits 2'. The spec defers not-run production (CAP-3). It does not say what replaces it: whether the other versions' already-finished child results are still appended, whether queued children still start, or whether the tmp dir is kept as `collect()`'s `rejected` path does today.
findings.implementation_impact: The child-exit-2 path is undefined in history mode. One implementation drops valid evidence from sibling versions, another appends it, and a third leaves orphan queued children running.
findings.suggestion: Define the interim behaviour: on the first child exit 2, start no further queued child, let in-flight children finish, append their records, append nothing for unstarted cells, and exit 2. Add a test.

findings.location: Boundaries > Always (ps-run-layer e2e history mode); cell-contract.md > Storage ('when the child left none')
findings.issue: Not covered: a child output that parses but fails today's checks in history mode. Today `collect()` rejects stray versions (exit 2) and `validate_layer_shape` failures exit 2 with the tmp dir kept. The contract only distinguishes a 'per-cell result' from 'none'. Also undefined: a payload whose `cells` lacks an admitted engine that was not probe-dropped, a payload with an extra engine, or `cells` present but malformed.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer must decide between exit 2 (no records, tmp kept) and `crash` records for each malformed shape, and the shape gate before merge may be dropped or kept arbitrarily.
findings.suggestion: List the outcomes: stray version or engine → exit 2 with tmp kept and nothing appended for that version; unparseable or shape-invalid output → `crash` for each admitted cell; missing engine not probe-dropped → `crash`.

findings.location: Boundaries > Always (ps-run-layer exit 143); Never ('`stopped` records' deferred); cell-contract.md > Storage
findings.issue: When ps-run-layer is stopped via `--stop-job` (JobStopped raised in its main thread, `_run()` returns 143), the contract appends a `stopped` record for each admitted cell. The spec defers `stopped` records without saying what to do instead: append nothing, append `crash`, or append results of children that already finished before the signal.
findings.implementation_impact: A stop mid-run could silently lose evidence that finished, or write `crash` records that later count toward the deferred blocked-infra rule.
findings.suggestion: State explicitly: on stop, append records only for children that already exited with a result, append nothing for in-flight or unstarted cells, print no output line, and exit 143.

findings.location: Boundaries > Always ('`ready` false unless every configured cell...' and Runner input errors); cell-contract.md > Runner > Input errors
findings.issue: The spec imports exit codes 'per Runner', but the contract's Runner input-error list mixes in-scope and deferred rules. In scope: neither/both of --cells/--versions; version repeated in --cells; cell outside the configured set; --per-version; psm_reports_dir equal to the module root; passthrough --screenshot-dir inside the module but outside psm_reports_dir; --cells with another layer. Contradicted or deferred: '--tier missing or other than 0/1' (spec: no --tier, tier null), '--jobs' is exit 2 (spec: --jobs stays), '--warm/--scenarios-from-failed'. The spec names only cells/versions and --per-version.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer must guess which input errors to enforce. Enforcing '--tier missing' would make every e2e run exit 2, and skipping the reports-dir/screenshot-dir checks lets screenshots written into the module stale the run's own fingerprint.
findings.suggestion: Enumerate the exact exit-2 cases for this slice, and state that --tier and --jobs are not checked (--jobs keeps bounding concurrent versions).

findings.location: Boundaries > Always (Plan's per-cell `rerun_matrix` and browser-keyed `layers.e2e`, 'both modes'); ps-plan-layers.py main canonical branch
findings.issue: Canonical mode has no `rerun_matrix` today (only `layers` + `rerun`; `per_version_rollup` runs only for --per-version). The contract says canonical `layers.e2e` is 'keyed by browser' and that `rerun` lists e2e while 'any configured cell has an e2e rerun_matrix entry'. It is undefined whether canonical mode gains a `rerun_matrix`, and what a browser-keyed canonical `layers.e2e[browser]` value means across three versions (reuse only if all versions pass? per-version nested?).
findings.implementation_impact: Two incompatible output shapes are possible, and tests or docs written against one break the other. The I/O row 'Narrowed plan' does not say which mode it covers.
findings.suggestion: Specify the canonical shape exactly, for example `layers.e2e = {<browser>: {<ver>: {reuse, reason, path}}}` plus a top-level `rerun_matrix` in both modes. State the per-version `layers.e2e[browser]` value shape too.

findings.location: Boundaries > Always (Plan rerun_matrix for every configured cell) vs Never (`phase1_reuse` deferred, CAP-1); references/run-phases.md Fase 1 ('`all_reuse` adalah gerbangnya')
findings.issue: The contract makes e2e `rerun_matrix` entries cover every configured cell whatever --versions, and keeps `all_reuse` 'today's computation' (`not matrix`). It says the real gates are `phase1_reuse` and `e2e_step`, both deferred here. Today Fase 1 for version V is gated on `all_reuse` of a `--versions V --per-version` plan. With this slice, any stale e2e cell of another version keeps `all_reuse` false, so V's Phase 1 loop can never end. The contract rule depends on the deferred `phase1_reuse` and the spec gives no replacement.
findings.implementation_impact: The documented Phase 1 loop either never terminates or the docs writer invents a gate. It also matters whether `all_reuse` is computed over the matrix (all cells) or over the per-version `rerun` lists (requested versions only).
findings.suggestion: State the interim Phase 1 gate (for example 'V's `per_version[V].rerun` is empty') and whether `all_reuse` counts out-of-scope e2e cells. Update run-phases.md accordingly.

findings.location: Boundaries > Never (headless config copy deferred); cell-contract.md > Headless + Configured cells; SPEC.md > Constraints (headless callers keep per-version verdict)
findings.issue: The contract keeps headless callers working because they write their versions and browsers into a config copy that becomes the configured set. This slice defers that copy but makes the configured set (from --config, resolver defaults 3×2) the only source of `ready`. A headless caller (psm-develop or psm-cross-version validating only 9.1) therefore always gets `ready=false` and `versions[1.7.8/8.1].ready=false`, a regression of its per-version verdict contract. The spec says nothing about this interim behaviour.
findings.implementation_impact: Shipping this slice breaks every headless caller's readiness signal until the CAP-1 headless slice lands, or the implementer improvises a config copy that the spec forbids ('do not half-build').
findings.suggestion: Decide the interim: either include the minimal headless config copy (`psm_target_versions`/`psm_e2e_browsers` written from caller args) in this slice, or state explicitly that headless callers get ready=false for unrequested versions and update headless.md and caller SKILL.md files to read only their versions' `versions[ver]`.

findings.location: Execution task 'docs' (SKILL.md Fase 1/2 e2e commands, run-phases.md); Never (tiers, `e2e_next_cells`, `e2e_step` deferred)
findings.issue: The contract's orchestration (run exactly `e2e_next_cells`, loop while `e2e_step` is gate, wrap-up) is deferred, but `--per-version` for e2e becomes exit 2 and `--browsers` becomes reserved. The spec gives no interim Fase 1/Fase 2 recipe: which cells each phase runs (`--versions V` = all configured browsers? the e2e `rerun_matrix` cells grouped into `--cells`?), when Fase 2 starts, and whether `--merge-only --layer e2e` stays gated by `all_reuse`.
findings.implementation_impact: The docs writer must design the interim workflow. Two writers would produce different command sequences, and the documented flow could re-run passing cells or never re-require Firefox.
findings.suggestion: Add a short interim recipe: Fase 1 = `ps-run-layer.py --layer e2e --versions V --session <t> --config …` when V's plan lists e2e; Fase 2 = `--cells` built from the e2e `rerun_matrix` entries; then `--merge-only --layer e2e` (no all_reuse gate) and the aggregate.

findings.location: Execution task 'docs' (e2e-quickstart.md TDD verdict step); cell-contract.md > Docs to update
findings.issue: The contract's quickstart verdict step is `ps-run-layer.py --layer e2e --cells … --tier 0 --session <token>`, but this slice adds no `--tier` flag. argparse would reject it with exit 2. The aggregate also needs `--module`, `--config` and a static file to produce a verdict. The spec does not give the slice's form.
findings.implementation_impact: Copying the contract's command into the docs produces a command that fails. Leaving out --config or the static input gives a misleading verdict.
findings.suggestion: Give the exact quickstart commands for this slice (no --tier; `--new-session` first; `ps-aggregate.py --reports-dir … --module … --config …`).

findings.location: Boundaries > Always (State, freshness, gate-grade; Plan reasons; Aggregate reasons) vs Never (CAP-1 Plan derivation)
findings.issue: Several in-scope rules depend on definitions in the deferred Plan derivation paragraph. Reason `not-gradeable` uses 'not-gradeable (below)' with authored_assertions 0, or scenario_notes equal to the plan's current `e2e_scenario_notes`. The aggregate reason `stale-fail` applies 'when the cell is failing (Plan)'. Per-version `e2e_state` uses 'newest gate-grade record is fail'. The spec does not say these definitions are in scope, or that 'failing' and 'not-gradeable' must be implemented while steps, focus and tiers are not.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer may skip `not-gradeable`/`stale-fail` as CAP-1 material, or half-build the derivation. Either way, reasons differ from the contract.
findings.suggestion: List explicitly that the 'failing' and 'not-gradeable' predicates from Plan are in scope (as functions), while steps, focus, tiers and next cells are not.

findings.location: Boundaries > Always (Aggregate reasons 'as in the plan'); cell-contract.md > Aggregate + Plan reasons `scenario-notes`/`not-gradeable`
findings.issue: The plan's `scenario-notes` vs `not-gradeable` split compares a record's `scenario_notes` with the *current* `e2e_scenario_notes`, which the plan derives live via `discover_scenarios` (including git-derived `deleted_specs`). The contract says the aggregate's `e2e_scenario_notes` 'comes from the selected records only'. So the aggregate has no 'current' notes to compare against, yet its reasons must match the plan's.
findings.implementation_impact: The aggregate and the plan can report different reasons for the same cell, or the implementer adds a live discover_scenarios/git call to the aggregate that the contract does not mention.
findings.suggestion: State whether the aggregate computes current notes live (and with which module path), or define its reason computation without that comparison.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Aggregate (`e2e_cells`, `versions[ver].reason`), referenced by Boundaries > Always
findings.issue: `e2e_cells[ver][browser] = {state, gate_grade, reason, findings, parallel_only}` has no defined `state` for a configured cell with no record (`missing`) or whose only lines are corrupt. `versions[ver].reason` is a single value, but a version has several cells, each possibly with a different reason. Nothing says which cell's reason wins, or whether it is a list or joined string.
findings.implementation_impact: The aggregate output shape is guessed, and acceptance criterion 2 ('e2e_cells names it with a contract reason') can be satisfied by several incompatible shapes.
findings.suggestion: Define: missing/corrupt cell → `state: null` (or 'missing'), `gate_grade: false`, `findings: []`. Define `versions[ver].reason` as either the first cell in browser order or a `{<browser>: reason}` map.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Plan reasons (`stale-tag`, `stale-source` (no fresh record))
findings.issue: When no record is fresh, the reason is `stale-tag` or `stale-source`, but the spec does not say which record decides it: the newest record, any record, or a record whose fingerprint matches but whose tag differs. A history with an old record on the current fingerprint but an old tag, and a newer record on an old fingerprint, has no defined answer.
findings.implementation_impact: Reasons become implementation-dependent, and tests asserting a specific stale reason are fragile.
findings.suggestion: Define it: judge from the newest valid record; `stale-tag` when its fingerprint matches but its tag differs, else `stale-source`.

findings.location: Execution task ps-plan-layers.py (`record_state`); cell-contract.md > State + incomplete-record rule
findings.issue: Records carry a stored `state` and `conclusive`, while State defines state from fields (not driven, errors, install.ok, launch_error, findings). The incomplete-record rule makes readers override a stored pass/fail. It is not said whether readers recompute state from the fields for every record (a stored `pass` with non-empty findings would read as `fail`) or trust the stored `state` except for the incomplete-record downgrade. 'Engine not driven' has no record-level test either.
findings.implementation_impact: Writer and reader can disagree, and `record_state` may be built as a pure reader of `state` or as a recomputation. That gives different results on legacy or hand-edited lines.
findings.suggestion: State that ps-run-layer computes `state`/`conclusive`/`reason` at merge time, and that readers apply only the corrupt and incomplete-record rules (or the reverse). Define 'not driven' (for example `started_at` set by ps-run-layer and no `browser:<engine>` phase).

findings.location: Boundaries > Always (Producers 'as written'); cell-contract.md > Evidence record > Producers ('Each finding gains `action` and `step`')
findings.issue: The contract requires each finding to carry `action` and `step` (the 0-based index in the spec's `steps`). `run_steps`/`_res` results today carry no step index, and `assemble_findings` emits id/severity/message/location/browser/scenario/source/versions only. Neither the spec's ps-e2e-run task nor the Code Map mentions this change, which touches `run_steps` and the universal smoke.
findings.implementation_impact: The change is easy to miss, and the later CAP-7 identical-findings comparison key (version, browser, scenario, step, action) has no data.
findings.suggestion: Add the item to the ps-e2e-run.py task: carry the step index through `run_steps` results into `assemble_findings` (`action`, `step`), and add a test.

findings.location: Boundaries > Always (ps-e2e-run.py child fields); cell-contract.md > Fields / Producers
findings.issue: The spec's child field list leaves out several contract fields: `scenarios_run` (spec `name` list), version-level `image_tag` (today the field is `tag`), and the null hooks `keeper_boot`, `scenario_spans`, `parallel_only`. 'keep hooks null/absent' does not say whether a field is written as null or omitted. It is also unclear whether the Fields list is closed (drop `boot_log`, `ps_domain`, `orchestrator`, `skipped_image`) or open.
findings.implementation_impact: Record shapes differ between implementations, and fixtures in tests must guess. A later slice that treats absent and null differently could misread these records.
findings.suggestion: Give the exact record key set for this slice: fields present with null for deferred hooks, `scenarios_run` = names of the full set run, `image_tag` renamed from `tag`, and whether extra fields are kept.

findings.location: Boundaries > Always (`ps-plan-layers.py --new-session`; plan and aggregate accept `--session` optionally) vs cell-contract.md > Fields ('passed as --session to every plan call ... both reject a missing or malformed token')
findings.issue: The contract requires `--session` on every plan call (missing → exit 2). The spec makes it optional for the plan. That is a contract change, not a deferral, and the frontmatter's 'Ask First: changing any contract rule' is not acknowledged. Separately, the spec says `ps-run-layer.py --layer e2e` requires `--session` unconditionally, while the contract exempts `--merge-only --layer e2e` ('--session do not apply').
findings.implementation_impact: An implementer following the spec literally rejects `--merge-only --layer e2e` without --session. One following the contract rejects plan calls without --session, and existing docs or tests break.
findings.suggestion: State that --session is optional for the plan in this slice, as a deliberate deviation, and that `--merge-only --layer e2e` neither requires nor accepts --session.

findings.location: Boundaries > Always (configured cells; `ps-run-layer.py --config` for every layer, `--config`/`--browsers`/`--engines` join RESERVED_PASSTHROUGH); SKILL.md On Activation step 2
findings.issue: The interactive scope menu narrows browsers via `--browsers` passed to every layer. After this slice, `--browsers` in ps-run-layer passthrough is exit 2, plan `--browsers` is deferred, and `--versions` for e2e always means all configured browsers. The spec's docs task does not cover SKILL.md On Activation step 2, so the documented way to narrow browsers breaks. Existing `-- --config …` passthrough usage (run-phases.md 'Teruskan --config … ke Lapis 1/2/4') also becomes exit 2.
findings.implementation_impact: The interactive flow gives an exit-2 error on its first narrowed E2E run, and the docs writer has to invent the replacement (`--cells`).
findings.suggestion: Add SKILL.md On Activation step 2 to the docs task: browser narrowing maps to `--cells`, and --config moves from passthrough to a ps-run-layer flag. Also update the ps-run-layer docstring example, which passes `--browsers` after `--`.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Runner > Input errors ('RESERVED_PASSTHROUGH (prefix abbreviations included)'); ps-run-layer.py `reserved_in_passthrough`
findings.issue: Today abbreviation detection is hard-coded to four flags ('--versions', '--output', '--progress-file', '--job-id'), with a minimum length of 4. The contract requires prefix abbreviations for every reserved flag. The spec adds `--config`, `--browsers`, `--engines` to the tuple but does not say the abbreviation loop must cover them. Short prefixes such as `--con` or `--br` collide with legitimate child flags (`--conf…` vs `--config`).
findings.implementation_impact: A literal implementation adds the names to the tuple only, so `--brow chromium` or `--conf x.json` slips through to the child and overrides ps-run-layer's own value.
findings.suggestion: State that the abbreviation check iterates over all of RESERVED_PASSTHROUGH, and define the ambiguity rule (match argparse's unique-prefix behaviour against the child's parser).

findings.location: Boundaries > Always (Configured cells; Bad config row); Execution task ps-flashlight-run.py (configured-cells reader)
findings.issue: The normalizer's input format is undefined. Resolver values are comma-separated strings ('1.7.8,8.1,9.1'), but a hand-written config may hold a JSON list. The spec also does not say whether whitespace or case is tolerated ('Chromium'), whether a config present without the key falls back to script defaults, or whether `--versions` of ps-run-layer (e2e) must match configured strings exactly, as `--cells` and the canary do.
findings.implementation_impact: Exit-2 behaviour differs between scripts, and the 'Bad config' test cannot be written unambiguously.
findings.suggestion: Specify: accept a string (comma-split, strip, lowercase engines) or a list of strings. A missing key → script default. `--versions` for e2e must match a configured string exactly, else exit 2.

findings.location: Boundaries > Always (State, freshness: `source_fingerprint`); cell-contract.md > Fresh
findings.issue: Fingerprint details are open. 'Every file' does not say whether symlinks (lstat entry, not followed) and directories, including empty ones, are entries. 'Top-level `.psm-*` files' does not say whether `.psm-*` directories are covered. `psm_reports_dir` is undefined for the plan and aggregate when no --config is given, and the plan's default `--reports-dir` is the relative `_bmad-output/psm-validate`. The 'reports dir equal to module root' error is assigned to the Runner only, leaving plan and aggregate behaviour undefined.
findings.implementation_impact: Plan, runner and aggregate can compute different fingerprints for the same tree, which makes every record read stale. The shared-function rule mitigates this only if all callers pass the same exclusion path.
findings.suggestion: Define the entry set (regular files and symlinks as lstat entries, no directories) and the exclusion (`realpath(--reports-dir)` when strictly inside the module). Make reports dir = module root exit 2 in all three scripts.

findings.location: Execution task ps-e2e-run.py ('boot timing wrapper measured after teardown') + Design Notes
findings.issue: The start point of the boot wall-clock is undefined: before the image-present check and `pull`, or at `bring-up`. Also unspecified: what the boot fields are when no boot happened (compose unavailable or skipped_image before bring-up) — empty `boot_phases` {} or null — and whether `boot_id` is still set. The port-conflict retry also yields `bring-up#2` and an extra `teardown`, which the spec does not mention.
findings.implementation_impact: Boot wall-clock numbers in the success-signal timing report depend on an arbitrary choice. Null/empty handling differs between child and aggregate.
findings.suggestion: Define it: the boot wall-clock spans from the image check (including pull) to the end of teardown. No container started → `boot_phases` {} (or null) and `boot_id` still the RUN_ID. Retries follow the #n rule.

findings.location: Boundaries > Always (Aggregate `--config`, versions replace `--versions`); cell-contract.md > Aggregate
findings.issue: 'A `--versions` that differs is an input error' does not define 'differs' (set, order, or string form such as 9.1 vs 9.1.0). The aggregate's E2E history reading needs `--reports-dir` + `--module`, and the spec does not say what happens when the aggregate is called with explicit `--static` and no `--reports-dir` (all cells `missing`, or exit 2). `e2e_screenshot_dir` = 'distinct run folders of the selected records' screenshots' requires deriving the `run-<ts>` ancestor from file paths, which is not specified.
findings.implementation_impact: Edge-case behaviour is guessed, and tests for the removed `unscanned` gate and the new versions source are underspecified.
findings.suggestion: Define 'differs' as set inequality after normalization. Require `--reports-dir`+`--module` for E2E (exit 2 otherwise, or all cells missing). Define the run folder as the first ancestor matching `run-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`.

findings.location: Execution task 'tests' ('contract-named tests in scope')
findings.issue: 'Contract-named tests in scope' is not enumerated, and some contract tests straddle deferred pieces. The Configured-cells test ('config 3×2 plus `--versions 9.1 --browsers chromium` still lists the other five cells as rerun') needs plan `--browsers`, which is deferred. The gate-grade test ('pass then fail ... gives ready=false and a step other than done') needs `e2e_step`, also deferred.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer must decide which assertions to drop or adapt. A reviewer cannot check completeness.
findings.suggestion: List the exact tests for this slice, and give the adapted form of the two straddling tests (`--versions 9.1` only; assert reason `fail` instead of step).

findings.location: Execution task ps-flashlight-run.py ('move `SUPPORTED_ENGINES`'); tests/test-ps-flashlight-run.py drift test
findings.issue: The spec moves `SUPPORTED_ENGINES` but does not say where the configured-cells defaults (`chromium,firefox`, `1.7.8,8.1,9.1`) live. The existing anti-drift test reads `DEFAULT_BROWSERS` from ps-e2e-run.py via ast and compares it to `PSM_DEFAULTS['psm_e2e_browsers']`. If the shared normalizer or reader owns the defaults, the test either silently guards a dead constant or breaks.
findings.implementation_impact: The single-owner rule for defaults is easy to violate, leaving two copies that can drift.
findings.suggestion: Say where the default browser and version lists live after the move, and update the drift test to read that owner.

findings.location: Acceptance Criteria 1 + Boundaries > Always (Honesty law)
findings.issue: Criterion 1 asserts that `ready` 'holds the E2E part true', but `ready` is a single boolean that also needs static conclusiveness (`version_ready` floor) and every `--require` layer. 'Counts each boot_id once' is trivially true of a dict keyed by boot_id. The Honesty law in Always says `ready` is false unless every configured cell passes, while the contract keeps `--require` without `e2e` as the way to gate without E2E.
findings.implementation_impact: The criterion is either untestable as worded or passes trivially. The Honesty-law sentence, read literally, contradicts the retained `--require` opt-out.
findings.suggestion: Rephrase criterion 1: with a conclusive static file for the 3 versions and `--require static,e2e`, `ready=true`, and `e2e_phase_durations[ver].boots` has exactly one key per distinct boot_id with the phases from one record. Add 'when `--require` includes e2e' to the Honesty-law line.

findings.location: Boundaries > Always ('Runner > Output' skipped rule); cell-contract.md > Runner > Output ('when `docker_available()` is false before slot counting')
findings.issue: The skipped rule is anchored to 'before slot counting', but slots are deferred. The spec does not say whether ps-run-layer itself probes `docker_available()` before spawning, or relies on children reporting `status: skipped`. Playwright-absent also only shows up from the child.
findings.implementation_impact: Two implementations differ in whether children are spawned without Docker. Output and exit code may differ when some children skip and others crash.
findings.suggestion: State: ps-run-layer calls `fl.docker_available()` before spawning any child; false → print `{e2e_status: skipped, ...}`, append nothing, exit 0. A child's skipped status is handled per the Output rule.

findings.location: Frontmatter `context` list
findings.issue: The spec says it delegates to the contract files, but `context` lists SPEC.md, cell-contract.md and brownfield.md, not tier-matrix.md. tier-matrix.md restates the `ready` definition and the 'empty tier 1 never makes ready true' rule.
findings.implementation_impact: Tooling that loads only `context` misses part of the contract. The impact is low, because the slice's rules are in cell-contract.md.
findings.suggestion: Add tier-matrix.md to `context`, or state that it is out of scope for this slice.

findings.location: Boundaries > Always ('`--per-version` is exit 2', 'writes no <module>-e2e*.json except --merge-only'); ps-plan-layers.py per_version_path / ps-aggregate.py --reports-dir derivation
findings.issue: Existing users have `<module>-e2e-<ver>.json` and `<module>-e2e.json` on disk, and the aggregate's reports-dir derivation auto-picks `<module>-e2e.json` today. The spec says these are ignored but does not say whether the new `--merge-only` view file (same name `<module>-e2e.json`, `view: true`) overwrites a legacy canonical file, or whether the aggregate must skip that name even when `--e2e` is not passed (rather than reject only explicit `--e2e`).
findings.implementation_impact: The aggregate may keep auto-loading the view file through the derivation loop and run it through `validate_layer_shape`/`e2e_layer`. That crashes or produces a wrong verdict.
findings.suggestion: State that the derivation loop in `ps-aggregate.py main` skips layer `e2e` entirely, and that the view write overwrites any legacy file of that name.
